To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

carriage of at least one allele of three studied SNPs of the promoter region at the TNF gene was associated with shorter time of onset of VAP and that this carriage was also associated with increased production of pro-inflammatory mediators by monocytes.
carriage of at least one allele A of the studied SNP is associated with shorter delay to development of V.A.P. and with greater production of pro-inflammatory mediators.
carriage of at least one allele of three SNPs in the TNF gene promoter is associated with a shorter time to development but not with disease severity of VAP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of genetic polymorphisms within the promoter region for the TNF gene for susceptibility to VAP in critically ill patients.
the genetic susceptibility to infections and more specifically to the role played by genetic polymorphisms of TNF gene for susceptibility to ventilatory-associated pneumonia.

the impact of genetic polymorphisms within the promoter region (at position -376, - 308, and -238) of the tumor necro-sis factor (TNF)-gene in the development of ventilator-associated pneumonia in critically ill patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
carriage of A alleles at the -376,-308 and -238 positions of the TNF promoter region is associated with a shorter time to develop VAP.
the presence of A alleles of the -376,-308 and -238 SNPs of the promoter region TNF gene is associated with an increased susceptibility to VAP.
the studied SNPs within the TNF gene are not associated with the development of VAP.
